purpose: A fixed games-only retrospective baseline (SMOOTHED_HISTORY_ODDS_V1) and its null comparison (NULL_HALF_V1) over every accepted 2016-2023 national FBS target of the BAT-711 history prefix, with immutable separate feature, estimate, label and score payloads and complete descriptive score summaries. Neither a favourable metric nor any improvement over the null is required; a correct unfavourable or null comparison is a complete delivery.

parent.read: the accepted history database (targets, history views, target_labels, exclusions) through the accepted history reader's full verification, plus the out_of_scope.jsonl payload of its own content identity (protected 2024/2025 contests, key and season only). No other parent, ranking, venue, market, held matrix, fitted weight, contaminated prediction or metric is read.
parent.semantics: accepted facts are reused under their original semantics; the history's exclusions (same-date and unsuitable prior observations) stay excluded with their reasons; the history contract is neither broadened nor rewritten; 2020 and postseason dates keep their parent season labels

split.rule: actual canonical-game membership outranks any supplied season label: a contest named by the accepted out-of-scope (2024/2025) payload is refused wherever it appears

SMOOTHED_HISTORY_ODDS_V1.formula: q_X = (W_X + T_X/2 + 1)/(G_X + 2) for each side X; p_A = q_A(1-q_B) / (q_A(1-q_B) + q_B(1-q_A)); p_B = 1 - p_A
SMOOTHED_HISTORY_ODDS_V1.cold_start: G = 0 gives q = 1/2 (flagged; the target is kept)

numeric_contract.integers: JSON integers only; a boolean or an integral float is not an integer; no binary float appears in any payload, record, meta value or identity document
numeric_contract.rationals: {numerator, denominator} JSON integers in lowest terms with denominator > 0
numeric_contract.decimal_display: probability_decimal and brier_decimal: the exact rational rounded half-even to 12 decimal places by integer arithmetic
numeric_contract.probability: exact rational; 0 < p < 1 always (smoothing); p_A + p_B = 1 exactly
numeric_contract.brier: (p_A - y)^2 exact rational; totals are exact rational sums and means are total / scored count
numeric_contract.log_loss: -ln(p_A) when y = 1 and -ln(1 - p_A) when y = 0, with p the correctly rounded binary64 of the exact rational and math.log of pinned CPython 3.12; serialized as repr() text
numeric_contract.log_loss_aggregation: math.fsum of the per-game binary64 values in canonical target order; mean = fsum / scored count (binary64); serialized as repr() text
numeric_contract.independent_tolerance: an independent recomputation of a transcendental (log-loss) value agrees within 1E-12 absolute; never applied to identity bytes, classification or rational fields
numeric_contract.canonical_json: json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) as UTF-8

population.targets: exactly the accepted history targets: 733, 753, 766, 769, 524, 767, 775 and 788 for 2016-2023 (5,875); expected membership is read from the accepted target table, never from delivered rows
population.views: exactly two oriented views per target (11,750): A = parent a side, B = parent b side
population.labels: exactly one separately classified label per target (5,875)
population.estimates: one record per target, model and orientation (23,500)
population.scores: one A-oriented record per target and model (11,750); mirrored rows are never scored
population.protected_rule: a target, contributing contest, excluded input or delivered record whose contest key is named by the accepted out-of-scope (2024/2025) payload, or whose season is outside 2016-2023, is refused (BENCHMARK_PROTECTED_KEY) whatever season label it carries

features.inputs: per side only its accepted same-season strictly earlier-date games G, wins W, losses L and ties T, with the exact contributing contest keys and the retained excluded inputs and reasons
features.verification: before use: counts are JSON integers (not booleans or integral floats), nonnegative and W + L + T = G; the contributing contests number G, each is an accepted history-pool contest of the same season involving that team, dated strictly before the target and never the target itself, with a result consistent with its points; W/L/T equal the contributing results; the contributing set equals every accepted pool contest of that team in that season dated before the target; history_state COLD_START exactly when G = 0; the two views are mirror images; a contest counted by both of its teams is mirrored; no protected key appears
features.date_bounds: calendar dates only; no midnight, retrieval time or publication time is turned into a historical known-at instant
features.target_site: display only; neither model reads it (no home bonus)

estimates.grain: target contest x model x orientation
estimates.rule: estimates depend only on the feature records and the frozen model definitions: each model is computed at game grain in A orientation from the A-view features, then both oriented rows are derived (p_B = 1 - p_A exactly); no label, score or target outcome is in scope; reordering inputs or changing a later, same-day or target label cannot change an earlier estimate
estimates.not_claimed: the comparison formula is a fixed illustrative rule, not an independently validated probability calibration; no confidence interval, calibrated uncertainty or credible pregame forecast is produced; ModelArtifact/FeatureVector are not used because no genuine training or forecast cutoff exists and none is fabricated

states.DECISIVE: y_a = 1 when the A side wins, 0 when it loses
states.TIE: explicit UNSCORED (LABEL_TIE); never a half label
states.UNSUPPORTED: explicit UNSCORED (LABEL_UNSUPPORTED): a label whose keys, date, season, integer points or results disagree

label_rules.consistency: a decisive or tied label that contradicts the points the accepted history later counts for the same contest is a refused input (BENCHMARK_LABEL_INPUT_INVALID), never a label choice

scores.grain: target contest x model, A orientation only
scores.join: the A-oriented estimate and the label joined by exact contest key; both record hashes are carried
scores.brier: (p_A - y)^2 exact rational with a 12-place half-even decimal display
scores.log_loss: -[y ln(p_A) + (1 - y) ln(1 - p_A)] as repr() text of the binary64 value
scores.unscored: tie, missing or unsupported labels stay explicit UNSCORED records with their reason; nothing is dropped, invented or half-scored and every denominator is exposed

summary.scopes: each season 2016-2023, each development partition (SPLIT-DEV-HIST 2016-2022, SPLIT-DEV-SEL 2023) and pooled 2016-2023, for both models
summary.fields: population targets, score records, scored and unscored targets (by reason), Brier total and mean (exact rationals and decimals), log-loss total and mean (repr text), cold-start target counts; per scope a descriptive smoothed-minus-null difference
summary.not_claimed: no blind evaluation, p-value, confidence interval, calibration, significance or predictive skill claim; both models are always reported even when the comparison is worse

outputs.payload_encoding: each record kind is one JSONL file of canonical lines in payload order, written as deterministic gzip (no file name, mtime 0, level 9); summary.json is one canonical line
outputs.payload_order: targets by (season, contest_date, contest_key); features by view A, B; estimates by model NULL_HALF_V1, SMOOTHED_HISTORY_ODDS_V1 then orientation A, B; scores by model

tables.meta: key/value: schema_version, contract_id, contract_sha256, content_identity, payload and uncompressed SHA-256s, row counts, parent, labels, split, models, numeric_contract, scope, summary
tables.blocks: one row per (record table, season) in the fixed layout features, estimates, labels, scores x 2016-2023: records, first/last record key, SHA-256 of the block's uncompressed JSONL lines and the zlib (level 9) block

database.determinism: page_size 4096, journal_mode OFF, rows inserted in layout order into a fresh file with no deletes and no VACUUM; content and physical SQLite bytes are reproducible under CPython 3.12.10, SQLite 3.49.1 and zlib 1.3.1
database.storage_reason: per-season compressed blocks keep the database about one tenth of a row-per-record layout, so the coordinated forgery family fits the issued cumulative storage allocation

identity_scheme.content_identity: sha256 of the canonical JSON content document {schema, stage: benchmark-content, population, contract_id, contract_sha256, parent, models: {id: sha256}, numeric_contract_sha256, payload_schema, outputs: {payload: sha256}, uncompressed_sha256, row_counts}
identity_scheme.database_identity: sha256 of the canonical JSON database document {schema, stage: benchmark-database, population, contract_sha256, content_identity, db_schema_version, outputs: {national_retrospective_baseline.sqlite: sha256}, table_counts} -- exactly these members
identity_scheme.comparison: identity documents are compared as canonical bytes: 13 and 13.0 are different documents
identity_scheme.immutability: create-only; an existing identity is verified and never rewritten; failed or superseded materializations stay immutable; no canonical default pointer changes

build.rule: every variant yields the same content identity, payload bytes and SQLite bytes; the committed contract precedes the first canonical write

refusals.rule: the reader re-derives every record from the accepted history and the frozen models before serving and refuses each defect for its own cause, in a fixed order: history location/identity (HISTORY_*, BENCHMARK_HISTORY_MISMATCH), benchmark location/manifest/bytes/identity, contract, meta claims (parent, PIT, protected, label, split, models, numeric contract, scope), table counts, block index columns and layout, protected keys and seasons, label leakage, feature count types, binary floats, mirrored score rows, duplicate/missing/extra/reordered records, record fields (PIT, label, split, model, orientation, team mapping, label, score, estimate, feature, source), summary, content identity, meta and the contract-defined identity document

consumer.selection: explicit --database <benchmark sqlite> and --history-database <accepted history sqlite>; never a default; no generic forecast consumer becomes active

filters.season: integer; outside 2016-2023 serves no rows with an explicit scope state
filters.team: org:<digits>, bare digits or a team name of that record's own season (casefolded); a name never resolves through another season or a global alias

consumer.paging: --limit/--offset/--all with exact totals in payload order; negative values, unknown or abbreviated flags and inapplicable filters refuse with exit 2
consumer.locations: BAT-717 literal read-only SQLite locations (long and extended-length Windows paths, reserved characters); a missing database is never created; network and device locations are refused
consumer.defaults: the five accepted query commands and their defaults are unchanged

non_claims: no PIT, known-at or publication-time authority; calendar order only
not a forecast; no predictive skill (NOT_ESTABLISHED) and no calibration
no fitting, tuning, hyperparameter selection, home advantage or favourable row selection
no 2024-2025 protected or 2026+ forward outcome is read, scored or labelled
no held Cycle 25.5 matrix, model, weight or metric is reused, corrected or reaccepted
no F1 completion, champion selection, activation, default change or hold release
